title: Spanish Roasted Pepper and Almond Romesco
description: Sweet roasted pepper, blanched almond paste and mild smoked paprika make a smooth romesco that stays thick without breadcrumbs.
equipment: Vitamix or immersion blender with tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: peeled roasted red bell pepper
ingredients.note: Plain home-roasted pepper with skin and seeds removed.

ingredients.name: fresh garlic cloves
ingredients.note: Peel and finely grate unless the step specifies otherwise.

ingredients.name: table salt
ingredients.note: Fine table salt, about 590 mg sodium per 1/4 teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1/16 tsp total.

steps.title: Soften the garlic
steps.text: Warm {ga} gently in {oil} in the HexClad for 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Bloom the tomato
steps.text: Stir in {to} and {pa} and cook for 30 seconds until brick red.

steps.title: Puree the romesco
steps.text: Take off the heat. Blend the tomato mixture with {bell}, {alm}, {rv}, {salt} and {w} until smooth and spoonable.

steps.title: Warm the finished sauce
steps.text: Return to low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until the almond and pepper thicken together.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Serve warm under flaky fish or alongside asparagus. The almond body makes it easy to spread a generous layer on the plate.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1/16 tsp table salt in place of 1/4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, halve the tomato paste and paprika and omit the vinegar. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 83 kcal, 2.3 g protein, 4.9 g total carbohydrate, 6.7 g fat, 1.5 g fiber, 152 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 83 kcal, 2.3 g protein, 4.9 g total carbohydrate, 6.7 g fat, 1.5 g fiber, 42 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
